data.description:
## Context / Problem

golden-busied-nag (Gerrit 3495, `d5f10d1d2c8`) made `rebar verify-opcert` read its `[verify]` settings from the project config committed on `origin/main`, never from the change under review. `docs/llm-framework.md` (the "Trust model" paragraph, around line 1063) still says the trust list lives "in the verifying environment's own `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` (never in the repository, ADR 0125)". It does not mention that the merge gate's project layer comes from main, so a reader of that page gets an incomplete, and for a repository-set list contradictory, account of where the gate's trust comes from. `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `docs/manifest-signing.md` and `infra/runbooks/mcp-opcert-enforcement-flip.md` were updated in that change; this page was missed.

## Approach

Amend the one sentence in that paragraph so it states both facts: the trust list belongs in the verifying environment's own configuration (ADR 0125), and when the merge gate runs, its `[verify]` settings and `tracker.dir` come from the project config committed on `origin/main`, never from the checkout under review, so a change cannot widen its own gate run. Keep the rest of the paragraph unchanged. Wording matches `docs/plan-review-gate.md` (the op-cert quote block) so the 2 pages agree.

Documentation only: no code, config key, env var or flag changes, so there is no new testable behaviour.

## Scope

- `docs/llm-framework.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The "Trust model" paragraph of `docs/llm-framework.md` states that `rebar verify-opcert` reads its `[verify]` settings from the project config committed on `origin/main`, not from the checkout under review: `grep -n "committed on \`origin/main\`" docs/llm-framework.md` prints a line in that paragraph.
- [ ] The paragraph still says the trust list belongs to the verifying environment (ADR 0125): `grep -n "verifying environment's own" docs/llm-framework.md` still matches.
- [ ] The docs gates pass: `pytest tests -k "docs" -q` and `make lint` exit 0.
data.title: llm-framework trust model omits the main-branch gate rule
